definition: Social deficit refers to an assumed shortfall in a person’s social abilities or understanding that is used to explain relationship or communication difficulties. In this source, that idea is challenged by the view that breakdowns can arise from a mutual mismatch in social expectations and behavior rather than from a deficit in one person alone.

reasons: The packet supports only a critique of attributing mixed-neurotype relational breakdowns to a deficit within the neurodivergent partner; it does not define “social deficit” more generally as a shortfall in social abilities or understanding causing relationship or communication difficulties.
The second sentence is broadly supported, but the first sentence adds an unsupported generalization beyond the source’s limited use of the term.
The packet does not define the term “social deficit” or describe it as an “assumed shortfall” in a person’s social abilities/understanding.

The packet discusses Milton’s “double empathy problem” as attributing relational breakdowns to “mutual misalignment in social expectations and behaviors,” but it does not explicitly frame this as “challenging the idea that social deficit explains relationship or communication difficulties.”
The definition asserts that this idea is “used to explain relationship or communication difficulties,” yet the packet does not support that characterisation of how “social deficit” is used.
